title: El curso de cocina
label: ch:es-curso
canDo: I can follow somebody explaining that a class did not suit them: hear that the level was too high, that they kept losing the thread, and that they moved to a beginners' group, and say the same about something of my own without criticising anyone.

payoff.summary: Follow two friends on a cooking class that was too advanced, then say the same about something of your own.
payoff.note: THIS IS THE FIRST CHAPTER TO TEACH WORDS THE AUDIT'S requires ROW DOES NOT LIST, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The row for mock 1 item 31 is `curso, grupo, avanzado, perderse, principiante, sencillo` -- all six are words of the AUDIO PASSAGE. The question's correct option reads `el nivel era demasiado alto para ella`, and BOTH `nivel` and `demasiado` have ZERO substring hits across spanish/lessons/ and spanish/units/. So the four ranked words clear the row while leaving the item unanswerable: a candidate who understood every word of the dialogue still cannot read option (b). Teaching six makes the item actually answerable, which is the stated goal, and the audit records the same one-item gain either way -- so this widening costs the metric nothing and is not number-chasing. Filed as BACKLOG.d HL-C421, which this chapter acts on for one item rather than fixing the instrument; repairing the rows corpus-wide moves the headline number and wants its own branch. NOTE the finding grew during authoring: HL-C421 was written on `nivel` alone, and `demasiado` was caught later by the token sweep, in MY OWN draft prose -- ES-C471-avanzado had written `un nivel avanzado` and the synthesis had used `demasiado` as if both were known. Two instances in one item, not one. FIVE RULES ALREADY OWNED, ALL CITED RATHER THAN RE-TAUGHT. (1) ES-C437-equivocarse AND ES-R437-repaso-planes BOTH name `perderse` explicitly, in the reflexive-of-misfortune family with caerse and olvidarse, and both say it is worth noticing as a group. So the rule is owned and only the SENSE is new: in a class you lose the THREAD, not the way. (2) ES-C09-estudiante (seq 965) owns -ante outright -- "Verb plus -ante = the person doing it", with the English -ant of participant, assistant, inhabitant -- so principiante is an instance, built in the lesson from principio via principiar. (3) ES-C282-invitado owns the participle-used-as-adjective move, so avanzado cites it. (4) ES-C60-bastante introduces ES-GRAMMAR-DEGREE-SCALE, so demasiado is presented as the missing member ABOVE the top of a scale the corpus already owns: poco below the point, bastante at it, demasiado past it. (5) ES-C359-litro already owns libra-latin and had taught lb, Libra the scales, deliberate and equilibrium -- so nivel takes roots: [libra-latin] and is a COUSIN of litro, libella being a little libra, with the l-to-n dissimilation through French named rather than glossed over. COUSIN LINKS CHOSEN SO THE JOIN KEY EARNS ITS KEEP: avanzado takes roots: [ante-latin], the slug ES-C323-antes holds, because avanzar is ab ante; demasiado takes [magis], the slug ES-C276-mas holds, because demasiado is de mas; principiante takes [principium-latin] from ES-C348-principio; perderse keeps perdere-latin from ES-C395-perder; nivel takes libra-latin from ES-C359-litro. Only singulus-latin is newly minted, for sencillo. SENCILLO IS NOT FACIL, and the lesson says so with a table: sencillo measures how few PARTS a thing has, facil how little EFFORT it costs. Climbing a staircase is sencillo and not facil. This matters for the item, because `hacemos cosas sencillas, pero las hacemos bien` is not modesty about effort -- it says the things have few parts and insists the execution is good. The -illo on sencillo is NOT a diminutive of anything synchronically: it was fused in the Latin singellus and there is no *senci underneath, and the lesson says that rather than letting the ending mislead. AVANZADO'S ENGLISH FACT: advance has an intrusive d, added on the false assumption that av- was a worn-down Latin ad-. Spanish never made that mistake, which is why avanzar has no d. TWO PREFLIGHT FAILURES FIXED PROPERLY RATHER THAN BY DELETION. sencillo and perderse each named an atom in practises that no body block assessed. sencillo's prerequisite moved from ES-C417-curso to ES-C398-facil, whose atom the Grammar Lens genuinely assesses and whose lesson it links to; perderse keeps ES-C471-sencillo as an ORDERING prerequisite without requiring its atom, since prerequisites establish sequence and requires establishes atom dependency. The synthesis then tripped the duration ceiling at 302s and the PROSE WAS TIGHTENED rather than the budget raised.
